ingredients: 1 small container low fat honey yogurt
2 or 3 cups fresh or thawed berries
steps: Blend together and serve.

recipes.title: Mango Cooler
steps: Combine mango puree, ice cream, tequila, and sugar in blender and blend well. Add ice cubes and blend until thick and frothy. Serve at once.

recipes.title: Orange Cooler
steps: Combine orange juice, wine, and sugar. Blend well. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice cubes and divide orange mixture among them. Fill glasses to top with ginger ale.

recipes.title: Orange Melon Wine Cooler
steps: Combine wine, melon puree, sugar, and lime juice and blend well. Chill thoroughly or serve over ice cubes.

recipes.title: Pineapple-Lychee and Rum Cooler
ingredients: 1 (20 oz) can seeded lychees in syrup
steps: Puree pineapple and lychees with syrup in blender. Add sugar and rum. Blend well. Blend ½ pineapple mix with 1 cup ice till frothy.
Repeat with other half of pineapple mix and ice cubes. Serve at once.

recipes.title: Strawberry Cooler
ingredients: 2 cups Muscat Alexandria or other sweet white wine
steps: Combine wine and strawberries in blender and puree. Strain. Add sugar and lime juice to wine mixture. Add ice cubes and blend till thick and frothy.

recipes.title: Cough Remedy
steps: Boil 20 min. Strain and drink.

recipes.title: Fruit Flavored Vinegar
steps: Heat sugar and vinegar. Pour over fruit in jar. Let set 5 days. Strain. Store.

recipes.title: Apple Caramel Thyme Loaf
recipes.note:
Keep the swirled caramel to 60 g. More than that and it sinks into a dense gummy layer at the bottom that the loaf cannot set around. The other 60 g goes on top after baking, where you can be as generous as you like.
Cool completely before slicing. Caramel-swirled quick breads are gummy while warm and slice clean once fully cold.
Dried thyme is about three times as strong as fresh, so 1.5 g dried replaces the 4 g fresh used in the scone version. That is roughly a rounded half teaspoon.
This is the loaf version of the Apple Caramel Thyme Scones. The second egg and the sour cream bind the crumb, and swirling the caramel instead of dicing it in keeps it from sinking into pockets.
Freeze-dried apple works if you would rather skip the pan step — 30 g crushed into the dry mix — but fresh gives the moist banana-bread texture.
ingredients: 250 g apple, peeled and diced small (Honeycrisp or Braeburn)
10 g butter, for cooking the apples
120 g sour cream or plain yogurt
steps: Cook the apples, heat the oven — Cook the diced apple in the butter over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes, until lightly browned at the edges and the pan is dry. Spread on a plate to cool. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a standard loaf pan, about 23 by 13 cm, with parchment.
Dry ingredients — Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and dried thyme together in a bowl.
Wet ingredients — In a large bowl, whisk both sugars, the eggs, oil, melted butter, sour cream, and vanilla paste until smooth and slightly thickened.
Combine — Fold the dry mix into the wet just until no streaks of flour remain. Do not overmix or the loaf turns tough. Fold in the cooled apples.

Layer and swirl — Scrape half the batter into the pan. Spoon 60 g of the caramel over it in a zigzag, then add the rest of the batter. Drag a knife through in an S-shape two or three times, just enough to marble, not blend.
Bake — 55 to 65 minutes, until a skewer in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs but no wet batter. Tent with foil for around 40 minutes if the top is browning too fast.
Cool and finish — Cool in the pan 15 minutes, then lift out by the parchment and cool completely on a rack. Warm the remaining 60 g of caramel, drizzle over the top, and finish with flaky sea salt.

recipes.title: Fresh Milled Tall Sandwich Loaves (Tangzhong Method)
recipes.note:
Fluffy, tall, soft sandwich bread using the Tangzhong method with freshly milled flour.
The tangzhong (flour paste) is the key to extra-tall, fluffy loaves — don't skip it. Finely mill your flour for best results. Dough should pass the windowpane test before bulk ferment.
Recipe from Generation Acres Farm.
ingredients: 65g freshly milled hard white wheat flour (tangzhong)
720g freshly milled hard white wheat flour
steps: Make tangzhong: whisk flour and water in small saucepan over medium heat. Stir constantly until thickened to pudding consistency (~5 min). Cool to room temp.
In stand mixer bowl, combine warm water, yeast, and honey. Let sit 5 min.
Add cooled tangzhong, flour, and salt. Mix with dough hook on low 2 min.
Add softened butter one tablespoon at a time while mixing.
Increase to medium speed, knead 8–10 min until smooth and pulls away from sides.
Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide dough in half. Shape each into a log and place in greased 9x5 loaf pans.
Cover and rise 45–60 min until dough crowns 1 inch above pan rim.
Preheat oven to 375°F.
Bake 28–32 min until deep golden brown and internal temp reaches 190°F.
Remove from pans immediately. Cool on wire rack at least 1 hour before slicing.

recipes.title: Easy Garlic Herb Focaccia with Fresh Milled Flour
recipes.note:
Golden, fluffy focaccia with a fragrant garlicky herb crust — great on its own, with soups, or as sandwich bread.
Fresh milled flour absorbs more water than store-bought. Dough will be very sticky — that's normal. The overnight cold ferment develops flavor and makes the focaccia extra airy.
Recipe from Generation Acres Farm.
ingredients: 600g freshly milled hard white wheat flour
steps: Combine warm water, yeast, and honey. Let sit 5 min until foamy.
Add olive oil, flour, and salt. Mix until shaggy dough forms.
Cover and rest 30 min, then perform 4 sets of stretch and folds every 30 min.
After final fold, cover and refrigerate overnight (8–12 hours).
Remove from fridge 2 hours before baking. Pour 2 tbsp olive oil into a 9x13 pan.
Transfer dough to pan. Gently stretch to fit. Proof 1.5–2 hours at room temp.
Preheat oven to 450°F. Make garlic herb oil by combining all topping ingredients.
Dimple dough with fingers, drizzle garlic herb oil over top, sprinkle with flaky salt.
Bake 20–25 min until golden brown. Cool 10 min before slicing.

recipes.title: Blackberry Vanilla Bean Scones
recipes.note:
Vanilla paste over extract — you get the visible seeds, a rounder flavor, and it does not thin the dough.
Small to medium berries go in whole. Halve large ones, and cut them frozen with a sharp knife, then straight back to the freezer. Cutting them thawed is what makes the mess.
Freeze-dried blackberries are the zero-risk version: crush 20 g into the dry ingredients for even, purple-free flavor. Or use both.
If the dough gets sticky and the berries start smearing, stop, chill everything 10 minutes, and resume. Streaks are a looks problem, not a flavor problem.
ingredients: 10 g flour, for tossing the berries
Glaze: 120 g powdered sugar, 22 g heavy cream, 4 g vanilla bean paste
steps: Dry mix and grated butter — Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl. Grate the frozen butter directly into the bowl on a box grater, tossing the shreds through the flour as you go so they stay separate.
Coat the berries — Toss the frozen blackberries with the 10 g of flour and put them back in the freezer until the moment you need them. The flour coat helps them hold their juice.
Whisk the wet — Whisk the cream, egg, and vanilla bean paste together until the seeds are evenly dispersed.

Combine, then fold in berries — Pour the wet into the dry and stir just until a shaggy dough forms with dry patches remaining. Add the frozen berries and fold no more than five or six times. The dough should still look undermixed.

Shape and freeze — Turn onto a floured surface and press, do not knead, into a disc about 2.5 cm thick. Cut into 8 wedges with a sharp knife, pressing straight down. Space on a lined sheet and freeze 20 minutes.
Bake — 205°C (400°F) for 20–22 minutes. They need a couple more minutes than plain scones because of the frozen fruit. Look for golden tops and dry-looking edges.
Cool and glaze — Cool at least 15 minutes so the berry pockets set. Whisk the glaze ingredients into a thick glaze and spoon over the tops.

recipes.title: Cheddar Herb Scones with Pickled Jalapeño
recipes.note:
Drain the jalapeños hard. Press them between paper towels until they stop weeping, or you will get wet spots in the crumb.
45 g of jalapeño reads as mild warmth. Go to 70 g if you want them to actually bite.
Grate cheddar from a block. Pre-shredded is coated in anti-caking starch that keeps it from melting properly.
Best the day they are baked — warm, split, and buttered.
ingredients: 45 g pickled jalapeños, drained and chopped
10 g mixed fresh herbs, finely chopped (5 g chives, 3 g basil, 2 g thyme)
25 g extra cheddar, for the tops
steps: Dry mix and grated butter — Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, and pepper together. Grate the frozen butter straight into the bowl on a box grater, tossing the shreds through the flour as you go.

Toss in cheese, peppers, herbs — Add the cheddar, jalapeños, and herbs. Toss with your hands until everything is coated in flour and evenly distributed. Doing this before the liquid goes in means the cheese will not clump.

Add the wet — Whisk the cream, egg, and pickling liquid together, pour into the dry mix, and stir just until a shaggy dough forms. It will look drier than a sweet scone dough; the cheese releases fat as it bakes.
Shape, top, and chill — Press into a disc about 2.5 cm thick, cut into 8 wedges. Space on a lined sheet, press the extra cheddar onto the tops, and freeze 15 minutes.
Bake — 205°C (400°F) for 20–22 minutes, until deep golden and the cheese on top has crisped into a lacy edge.

recipes.title: Delicious Buttery Flaky Fresh Milled Biscuits
recipes.note:
Flaky, buttery biscuits that rise nicely using your own fresh milled flour.
Works with kamut, einkorn, or soft/hard white wheat. Cold butter is essential for flakiness.
Recipe from Generation Acres Farm / Kristin.
ingredients: 360g finely milled kamut, einkorn, or soft white wheat
240g buttermilk (or milk + 14g white vinegar, let curdle 5 min)
steps: Preheat oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Combine dry ingredients in large bowl.
Grate in cold butter and mix with hands until covered in flour and resembles coarse sand. Rub between hands to fully incorporate.
Add buttermilk and mix until combined.
Turn out onto floured surface and knead a few times. Roll to about ½" thick and cut dough in half.
Place one half over the other and gently roll together — don't flatten too much.
Cut biscuits with a sharp biscuit cutter and place on parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake 10–12 min until golden brown. Brush tops with melted butter if desired.

recipes.title: Fresh Milled Buttermilk Biscuits
recipes.note:
These fresh milled buttermilk biscuits are just 6 ingredients yet dangerously delicious!
Equipment: 1 Rolling pin; 1 Mixing bowl; 1 Cast iron or baking pan; 1 2 inch to 3 inch Biscuit cutter or glass
Cold butter is the secret to flaky layers — don't let it warm up. Soft white wheat produces a more tender biscuit than hard wheat. Kefir works perfectly as a buttermilk substitute.
Recipe from Lovely Bell Bakes.
ingredients: 300g fresh milled soft white wheat flour, plus extra for dusting
113g salted butter, cold (freeze 20 min before using)
steps: Put butter in freezer for at least 20 min before starting.
Preheat oven to 450°F. Lightly flour a work surface.
Whisk together flour, salt, and baking powder in a large bowl.
Grate frozen butter directly into flour mixture using a cheese grater. Toss to coat.
Add honey to buttermilk and stir. Pour into flour-butter mixture.
Mix gently with a fork until just combined — do not overmix. Dough will be shaggy.
Turn onto floured surface. Gently press into rectangle, fold in thirds, rotate 90°, repeat 3–4 times.
Pat dough to ¾ inch thickness. Cut with biscuit cutter — press straight down, no twisting.
Place on cast iron or baking pan. Let rest 15 min in fridge.
Bake 18–20 min until golden brown on top.
Mix honey and butter, brush over hot biscuits immediately.

recipes.title: Lemon Basil Scones
recipes.note:
The zest-rubbing step is the whole recipe. Skip it and you get flecks; do it and you get lemon in every bite.
For even louder lemon, swap 15 g of the cream for lemon juice. It will curdle slightly, which is fine and tenderizes the crumb.
Frozen butter grated on a box grater gives the flakiest layers.
Do not skip the chill before baking. It is the difference between tall scones and flat ones.
Basil is featherlight. 12 g is roughly a small handful of leaves before chopping.
ingredients: 12 g fresh basil leaves, finely chopped
113 g unsalted butter, cold and cubed
Glaze: 120 g powdered sugar, 20 g lemon juice
steps: Wake up the zest and basil — Put the sugar in a bowl with the lemon zest and chopped basil. Rub together with your fingertips for a full minute until the sugar is damp, pale green, and smells intensely of lemon. This is where most of the flavor comes from; do not rush it.
Mix the dry ingredients — Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt into the scented sugar.
Cut in the butter — Work the cold butter in with your fingers or a pastry cutter until the pieces are pea-sized. Leave some larger flakes; they make the layers.
Add the wet — Whisk the cream, egg, and lemon juice together, then pour into the dry mix. Stir just until it comes together in a shaggy mass. Overworking makes them tough.
Shape and chill — Turn out onto a floured surface, pat into a disc about 2.5 cm thick, and cut into 8 wedges. Space on a lined sheet and freeze 15 minutes.
Bake — 205°C (400°F) for 18–20 minutes, until the tops are golden and the edges are set.
Cool and glaze — Cool at least 10 minutes. Whisk the powdered sugar with the lemon juice until pourable but still thick, spoon over the scones, and finish with flaky salt.

recipes.title: Rosemary Parmesan Scones
recipes.note: Cold butter is key for flaky layers. Soft white wheat keeps these tender. Extra parmesan on top before baking adds a nice crust.
ingredients: 240g fresh milled soft white wheat flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl.
Cut in cold butter with a pastry cutter or your fingers until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in parmesan and rosemary.
In a small bowl, whisk together egg and buttermilk. Pour into flour mixture.
Mix until just combined — do not overmix. Dough will be shaggy.
Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and gently bring together into a disc about 1 inch thick.
Cut into 8 wedges and place on prepared baking sheet.
Bake 12–15 minutes until golden on top and firm to the touch.
Cool 5 minutes before serving. Best warm.

recipes.title: Soft Vanilla Cinnamon Rolls (Fresh-Milled)
recipes.note: Sift flour once and remove ~30–55g coarse bran for maximum fluff. Quick timeline: shape at 8:30–9:30pm, fridge overnight, pull at 8:15am, bake at 10:00am.
steps: AUTOLYSE: Mix flour + 300g warm milk until no dry flour. Cover and rest 25 min.
Stir yeast into remaining 40g warm milk. Let sit 5–10 min until foamy.
Add yeast mixture, sugars, eggs, vanilla, and milk powder to autolysed dough. Mix until combined. Add salt and mix 30 seconds.
Add softened butter in pieces, mixing/kneading until incorporated.
Knead 6–8 min. Dough should be soft, elastic, slightly tacky.
Place in lightly greased bowl, cover. Rise 60–90 min until doubled.
Mix filling: softened butter + brown sugar + cinnamon + vanilla + pinch salt into a paste.
Roll dough into ~18x12" rectangle, ¼" thick. Spread filling evenly to edges.
Roll up tightly from long edge. Slice into 12 rolls.
Place rolls in greased 9x13 pan. Let sit at room temp 10–20 min, then cover and refrigerate 8–12 hours.
BAKE DAY: Remove from fridge, let sit covered 60–90 min until puffy.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Bake 22–28 min until lightly golden (center should reach 190–195°F).
Beat cream cheese + butter until smooth. Add vanilla, salt, powdered sugar, and milk to pouring consistency.
Cool rolls 5–10 min, then spread glaze over warm rolls.

recipes.title: Boston Cream Pie
steps: ## Make the Cake
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9-inch round cake pan.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, beat eggs and sugar until light and fluffy.
Heat the milk and melted butter until warm, then stir in vanilla.
Gradually fold the dry ingredients into the egg mixture. Stir in the warm milk mixture until smooth.
Pour into the prepared pan and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Let the cake cool completely before slicing in half horizontally.
## Make the Pastry Cream
Heat the milk over medium heat until steaming (but not boiling).
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch until smooth.
Slowly whisk the hot milk into the egg mixture, then return everything to the pot.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened (about 2-3 minutes).
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla and butter.
Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface and refrigerate until cool.
## Make the Ganache
Heat the heavy cream until hot but not boiling.
Pour over chopped chocolate and butter. Let sit for a minute, then stir until smooth.
## Assemble the Pie
Place one cake layer on a plate and spread the pastry cream evenly over it.
Place the second cake layer on top.
Pour the ganache over the top, letting it drip slightly over the edges.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Honey Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)
recipes.note:
Cinnamon doesn't infuse into honey very well, so steeping it in the milk is what carries the flavor. For just a hint of cinnamon, skip the steep and use only the honey.
Steep off the burner. Leaving the milk on low the whole time risks scorching it.
90 g honey is about 4 tablespoons. Set the hot bowl on a folded towel on the scale before taring.
ingredients: 2 cinnamon sticks, snapped into pieces (or 2 g ground cinnamon)
steps: Steep — Heat the milk, cream and cinnamon pieces until steaming, with small bubbles at the edge. Do not boil. Take it off the burner, cover, and steep 20 minutes.
Reheat — Strain out the cinnamon, add 33 g of the sugar and the salt, and bring back up to steaming.
Whisk the yolks — Whisk the yolks with the remaining 32 g sugar until pale.
Temper — Slowly whisk a ladle of the hot milk into the yolks, then pour everything back into the pot.
Cook the custard — Stir over low heat until it coats a spoon, 77–80 °C.
Add the honey — Strain the custard into a bowl set on the scale, tare it, and stir in 90 g cinnamon honey off the heat.
Chill and freeze — Cool, divide between 2 pints up to the max line, and freeze level for 24 hours. Spin on the Ice Cream setting.

recipes.title: Homemade Lemon Curd
recipes.time: Prep 10 minutes · Cook 10–15 minutes · Chill at least 1 hour
recipes.note:
Keeps up to 1 week in the fridge.
Recipe from August 1st Desserts, for the Lemon Tiramisu.
ingredients: ¼ cup fresh lemon juice (about 2 lemons)
4 tbsp (½ stick) unsalted butter, cut into small cubes
steps: Set up a double boiler (or heatproof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water). Water should not touch the bottom of the bowl.
Whisk ingredients: In the bowl, whisk together egg yolks, sugar, lemon juice, zest, and salt until smooth.
Cook over simmering water: Stir constantly with a rubber spatula or whisk. Cook 10–15 minutes, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon. Don't let it boil.
Add butter: Remove from heat. Stir in butter cubes until fully melted and smooth.
Strain (optional): For extra smooth curd, strain through a fine mesh sieve into a bowl.
Cool & chill: Press plastic wrap directly on the surface to prevent a skin. Chill for at least 1 hour.

recipes.title: Lemon Custard (Dairy-Free)
recipes.note: Tart custard suitable for pavlova or dessert fillings. Thickens further as it cools.
steps: In a saucepan, whisk together lemon juice, coconut milk, sugar, tapioca flour, lemon zest, and salt.
Heat over medium heat until warm.
In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks.
Slowly add a small amount of warm liquid into egg yolks while whisking to temper.
Pour egg mixture back into the saucepan.
Cook over medium heat while stirring continuously until custard thickens.
Once thickened, remove from heat and allow to cool.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.

recipes.title: Lemon French-Style Cheesecake with Lemon Curd and Whipped Cream Rosettes
recipes.time: Bake crust 8–10 minutes, cheesecake 40–45 minutes · Chill at least 4 hours or overnight
recipes.note:
Serving Tips:
For clean slices, wipe knife between cuts.
Store cheesecake covered in the fridge for up to 5 days.
ingredients: ½ cup fresh lemon juice (about 2–3 lemons)
6 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into pieces
1 cup heavy whipping cream, very cold
steps: ## Prepare the Crust
Preheat oven to 325°F (163°C).
Mix graham cracker crumbs, sugar, and melted butter.
Press firmly into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, then let cool.
## Make the Cheesecake Filling
Beat cream cheese until smooth.
Add sugar and mix well.
Add vanilla, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
Beat in eggs one at a time until just combined.
Fold in sour cream gently.
## Bake the Cheesecake
Pour filling over cooled crust.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, until center jiggles slightly.
Turn off oven, crack oven door, and let cheesecake cool inside for 1 hour.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
## Make the Lemon Curd
In a saucepan, whisk lemon juice, zest, sugar, and eggs.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened (5–7 minutes).
Remove from heat and stir in butter until smooth.
Strain if desired for extra smoothness.
Cool and refrigerate.
## Assemble the Cheesecake
Spread cooled lemon curd over chilled cheesecake.
Chill cheesecake again for 30 minutes to set the curd.
## Make Whipped Cream Rosettes
Beat cold heavy cream to soft peaks.
Add powdered sugar and vanilla, beat to firm peaks.
Pipe rosettes around the edge of cheesecake using a star tip.

recipes.title: Lemon Tiramisu with Lorna Doone Shortbread
recipes.note:
Served with the Homemade Lemon Curd and Thick Raspberry Topping from the same August 1st dessert set.
Recipe from August 1st Desserts.
ingredients: 3–4 tbsp melted butter (just enough to lightly bind crumbs)
½ to 1 cup lemon curd (homemade or store-bought) — see Homemade Lemon Curd
Fresh whipped cream or cream cheese whipped cream
Lemon zest, Lorna Doone cookie crumbles, or edible flowers
steps: Prepare shortbread base: Crush Lorna Doone cookies into fine crumbs. Mix with melted butter and press lightly into the bottom of your pan or dessert cups. Chill while you prepare the rest.
Make limoncello syrup: In a small saucepan, bring water and sugar to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat and stir in limoncello and lemon zest. Let cool slightly.
Whip the cream: In a separate bowl, whip the heavy cream until soft peaks form. Set aside.
Prepare mascarpone filling: Beat mascarpone, cream cheese, powdered sugar, vanilla, zest, and limoncello until smooth. Gently fold in the whipped cream until fully combined and fluffy.

Assemble: Layer: cookie crust → brush with limoncello syrup → mascarpone cream → thin layer of lemon curd (optional). Repeat if desired (in a trifle or deep dish). Finish with a final mascarpone layer or whipped topping.
Chill: Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight for best flavor and texture.
Garnish before serving: Top with extra whipped cream, lemon zest, cookie crumbles, or edible flowers.

recipes.title: Muffin Tin Pie Bites (Pumpkin + Caramel Apple)
recipes.note: Mini pies baked in a standard muffin pan. One batch of dough makes 26 shells: 13 pumpkin and 13 caramel apple, plus a frozen piece for grating over the apple bites.
ingredients: 250 g ice water (200 g to start, the rest only if needed)
240 g evaporated milk or heavy cream
1 kg apples, peeled and diced about 1 cm (Granny Smith or a Granny Smith and Honeycrisp mix)
70 g brown sugar (100 g if skipping the caramel)
120 g heavy cream, room temperature (evaporated milk works too; simmer a little longer)
steps: ## Shared Pie Dough
Whisk the flour, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Cut the butter into the flour until the pieces are pea-sized, with a few larger bits left. Keep everything cold.
Beat the egg into 200 g of the ice water.
Drizzle the egg-water in gradually, tossing with a fork, until the dough holds together when squeezed. Add reserved water only if needed. Do not knead.
Pull off about 200 g as a disc for grating and freeze it. Split the rest into 3 flat discs, wrap tightly, and refrigerate overnight (at least 1 hour).
Let the fridge discs sit 10 to 15 minutes before shaping.
## Shaping the shells
Grease the muffin cups well.
Weigh about 48 g of dough per shell.
Drop a ball into each cup and press it down and out with a floured tamper or lemon press so the dough climbs the sides. Thumb the edges up to the rim.
Thin out the dough where the bottom meets the side so the corners don't stay doughy.
Chill the pan 15 minutes before baking. Dough keeps 2 to 3 days in the fridge.
## Make the fillings
Pumpkin filling: Whisk everything until smooth. The filling keeps up to 2 days in the fridge; whisk again before pouring.

Apple filling: Melt the butter in a large pan, add everything else, and cook over medium heat 6 to 8 minutes, until the apples just start to soften and the juices thicken. Cool completely. Keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

Caramel sauce: Melt the sugar in a heavy pan over medium heat, swirling rather than stirring, until deep amber. Whisk in the butter. Off the heat, slowly whisk in the cream (it will bubble hard). Stir in the salt and vanilla and let it cool until thick. Keeps about 2 weeks in the fridge; warm it briefly to loosen.
## Pumpkin Pie Bites
Par-bake: line each chilled shell with a liner or parchment, fill with dried beans or rice, and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove the weights and bake 3 to 5 minutes more, until the bottoms look dry and the edges are lightly golden.
Optional: brush the insides with beaten egg white and bake 1 minute to seal.
Lower the oven to 175°C (350°F). Fill the warm shells nearly to the top.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the centers barely jiggle. Pulling them a couple of minutes early reduces puffing.
Cool in the pan 15 to 20 minutes, run a thin knife around each, and lift out. Cool completely on a rack, then refrigerate.
## Caramel Apple Pie Bites
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) with a sheet pan inside.
Spoon about 7 g of caramel into the bottom of each unbaked shell.
Mound the apple filling on top.
Grate 15 to 20 g of the frozen dough loosely over each one, so some filling still shows.
Set the muffin pan on the hot sheet pan to catch drips and crisp the bottoms. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
Cool 10 to 15 minutes, then run a thin knife around each and lift out before any leaked caramel hardens. If one sticks, warm the pan in the oven for a minute.
Once warm rather than hot, drizzle with more caramel and sprinkle a few flakes of vanilla salt while the drizzle is still tacky.

recipes.title: One-Pot Caramel — Sauce and Chewy Bits
recipes.makes: about 200 g sauce and 400 g cuttable caramel
recipes.note:
Calibrate the thermometer first. Boiling water should read 100°C. A few degrees off is the difference between sauce and candy.
Temperature landmarks: 105°C is pourable syrup, 112°C is thick sauce that sets soft, 118°C is chewy and cuttable, 124°C goes hard and brittle.
Constant stirring is not optional. A silicone spatula that reaches the pan corners beats a whisk here.
Have the jar and a ladle ready before starting. At 112°C the temperature climbs fast.
The bits keep 3 weeks at room temperature wrapped, or indefinitely frozen. The sauce keeps 2 weeks refrigerated and needs warming before it will drizzle.
steps: Set up first — Line a loaf pan with parchment, leaving overhang on two sides, and butter the parchment. Set out a heatproof jar for the sauce portion. Clip a candy thermometer to a heavy-bottomed pot, tip not touching the bottom. Do all of this before turning on any heat.

Melt everything together — Put the sugar, condensed milk, butter, corn syrup, cream, and salt in the pot. Melt over medium-low, stirring, until smooth and the sugar no longer feels gritty against the pan bottom.
Bring to a boil — Raise to medium and bring to a steady boil. From here on, stir constantly, scraping the bottom and into the corners the whole time. The milk solids will scorch the second you stop.
First pull at 112°C — the sauce — When the thermometer hits 112°C, immediately pour off about a third, roughly 200 g, into the jar. Stir 3 g of the vanilla paste into the jar and set aside.

Take the rest to 118°C — Return the pot to the heat and keep cooking the remainder, still stirring constantly, until it reaches 118°C. It will darken and thicken noticeably and the bubbles will get slower and heavier.

Pour out the chewy caramel — Off the heat, stir in the remaining 3 g of vanilla paste, then pour into the lined loaf pan. Do not scrape the very bottom of the pot into the pan; that is where any scorched bits collect.
Cool completely — 2–3 hours at room temperature, or 1 hour in the fridge, until fully firm. Cutting warm caramel just smears it.

Cut and store the bits — Lift out by the parchment. Cut into 6 mm cubes with a buttered knife, wiping the blade between cuts. Toss the cubes with a spoonful of flour so they do not stick together, then freeze until needed.

recipes.title: Thick Raspberry Topping (Spoonable & Lush)
recipes.note: Recipe from August 1st Desserts, for spooning onto the Lemon Tiramisu.
ingredients: Optional: splash of Limoncello or raspberry liqueur (for depth)
steps: Simmer the berries: In a saucepan, combine raspberries, sugar, and lemon juice. Cook over medium heat until berries start to break down (5–7 minutes).
Thicken: In a small bowl, mix cornstarch and water to create a slurry. Stir slurry into the hot raspberry mixture. Simmer another 2–3 minutes, stirring often, until thick and glossy.
Optional—strain for smoothness: Strain through a fine mesh sieve to remove seeds, or leave them for texture.
Liqueur finish (optional): Stir in 1–2 tsp of Limoncello or raspberry liqueur off the heat for added flavor.
Cool completely: Let it cool to room temp, then chill before spooning onto your tiramisu.

recipes.title: Triple Chocolate Pistachio Bread
recipes.note:
Moist, soft, sweet pistachio bread, jam-packed with a TON of chocolate! Even chocolate streusel!
Do not cool completely in the pan — it will stick! Ganache sets quickly once at room temp.
Recipe from The Gold Lining Girl / Sarah.
ingredients: 1 box white or yellow cake mix (~432g)
1 box instant pistachio pudding mix (96g / 3.4 oz)
steps: Stir together cake mix, pudding mix, eggs, sour cream, oil, and 255g chocolate chips. Mixture will be thick.
Spread half the batter into a well-greased bundt or tube pan.
Whisk together sugars, cocoa powder, and cinnamon for streusel.
Sprinkle half the streusel over the batter. Swirl lightly with a knife.
Spread remaining batter. Sprinkle with remaining streusel and swirl lightly.
Bake at 350°F for 40–50 min, or until edges are golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 10 min, then run a knife around edges and invert onto a serving plate. Cool completely.
For ganache: combine chocolate chips, heavy cream, and butter. Microwave in 20-second intervals, whisking until smooth.
Drizzle ganache over cooled bread. Sprinkle with remaining 85g mini chocolate chips.
Allow 10–15 min for ganache to set. Cut and serve.

recipes.title: Vanilla Bean Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)
recipes.note:
Keep the custard under about 82 °C or the yolks start to scramble.
Homemade paste varies in strength. Start with 16 g, taste the warm base, and add more if needed.
Save the 4 egg whites for the Pavlova.
steps: Heat the dairy — Warm the milk, cream, 65 g of the sugar and the salt until steaming, with small bubbles at the edge. Do not boil.
Whisk the yolks — Whisk the yolks with the remaining 65 g sugar until pale.
Temper — Slowly whisk a ladle of the hot milk into the yolks, then pour everything back into the pot.
Cook the custard — Stir over low heat until it coats a spoon, 77–80 °C. A double batch takes a few extra minutes.
Finish — Off the heat, stir in the vanilla paste, then strain into a bowl.
Chill and freeze — Cool, divide between 2 pints up to the max line, lid, and freeze level for 24 hours.
Spin — Run on the Ice Cream setting. Respin with a splash of milk if it comes out crumbly.

recipes.title: Apple Barbecue Sauce
recipes.note:
Skim the fat off the pan juices before measuring them.
If the pork isn't done yet, use apple cider in place of the pan juices.
Thin with a little more pan juice or cider if it gets too thick.
ingredients: 60 g reduced pan juices from the pulled pork (or apple cider)
steps: Combine — Stir everything together in a small saucepan.
Simmer — Simmer 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Adjust — Taste and adjust with more sugar for sweetness or vinegar for tang.
Serve — Serve warm on the side with the Apple Cider Pulled Pork.

recipes.title: Apple Cider Pulled Pork
recipes.note:
Plan about 225 g raw pork per person. It loses roughly 40–50% of its weight as it cooks.
Bone-in is usually cheaper per pound, and the bone is about 10% of the weight. Boneless works too.
Avoid loin or tenderloin. They are too lean and dry out instead of shredding.
Makes ahead well. Reheat the shredded pork in its juices.
Save some reduced pan juices for the barbecue sauce.
ingredients: 2 kg bone-in pork butt (Boston butt or shoulder blade roast, about 4.5 lb)
Apple spice pork seasoning, enough to coat generously
240 g apple cider, for the pan
15 g apple cider vinegar, to finish
Apple Slaw and Apple Barbecue Sauce, to serve
steps: Season — Pat the pork dry and coat it all over with the seasoning.
Set up — Put the pork fat side up in a foil pan with the apple cider in the bottom. Heat the smoker to 107–121 °C (225–250 °F).
Smoke — Smoke 7–9 hours. Around 71 °C the temperature can stall for a couple of hours. Cover the pan with foil to push through it.
Check — It is done at 90–95 °C inside, when a probe slides in like butter and the bone wiggles loose.
Rest — Rest covered for 30–60 minutes.
Reduce the juices — Pour off the pan juices, skim the fat, and simmer a few minutes to reduce.
Shred and toss — Shred the pork and toss with some of the reduced juices, the cider vinegar and a pinch more seasoning.
Serve — Pile onto toasted potato buns with slaw and jalapeños, with barbecue sauce on the side.

recipes.title: Apple Slaw with Cider Dressing
recipes.note:
Pink Lady browns slowly and Sugarbee stays crisp and juicy raw. Fuji works but is sweeter.
Keep the dressing vinegar-forward when serving with apple-spiced pork. Skip dried fruit and cinnamon.
Toasted nuts, fennel or celery add extra crunch.
ingredients: 400 g cabbage, shredded (red and green, just under half a medium head)
200 g apple, julienned (1 large Pink Lady or Sugarbee)
30 g olive oil (or 60 g mayo for a creamy slaw)
steps: Prep the vegetables — Shred the cabbage and carrot and slice the onion. These can be done a day ahead and kept in a bag in the fridge.
Make the dressing — Whisk or shake everything for the dressing in a jar. It keeps in the fridge too.
Cut the apple — Julienne the apple and toss it with a little of the dressing right away so it doesn't brown.
Toss — Toss everything together a few hours before serving and chill.
Serve — Serve on the side or piled onto pulled pork sandwiches.

recipes.title: Butternut Squash Soup
recipes.note:
Don’t skip roasting — boiling makes the squash taste watery. Roasting concentrates and caramelizes it.
Brown butter instead of regular butter adds nutty depth without competing with the squash.
A tiny drizzle of maple syrup at the end (½ tsp) brightens the natural squash sweetness.
Garnish with toasted pepitas and a swirl of cream.
No red pepper — keep it pure squash!
Link saved at the end of the original file: https://simplygoodcooker.com/alex-green-vanilla-bean-paste-recipe/
ingredients: 1 large butternut squash (about 3 lbs), halved and seeded
Salt and white pepper to taste
steps: Roast the squash — Brush the cut sides with olive oil, season with salt, and roast cut-side down at 400°F for 45–50 minutes until deeply caramelized. This is where the flavor lives.
Sauté aromatics — Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Build the soup — Scoop the roasted squash flesh into the pot. Add broth and bring to a simmer for 10 minutes to meld the flavors.
Blend — Use an immersion blender (or transfer in batches to a blender) and purée until silky smooth.
Finish — Stir in cream if using, add nutmeg, and season well with salt and white pepper. Thin with more broth if needed.

recipes.title: One Pan Jambalaya
recipes.note:
Easy, healthy comfort food made in just one pan, loaded with chicken, sausage, veggies, and bold cajun flavors.
*Sausage: I substitute Polska Kielbasa sausage when cooking for my family, because it's less spicy for my kids.
Shrimp: Jumbo, uncooked shrimp could be thrown in the same time as the rice and cooked with everything together. Or you could cook the shrimp separately (or thaw frozen cooked shrimp) and add it at the end.
Gluten-free Adaptations: use gluten-free all-purpose flour.
Recipe from Tastes Better From Scratch / Lauren Allen.
ingredients: 1 pound andouille sausage*, cut into 1/4 inch thick slices
1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-size pieces
1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional, add more for spice, if desired.)
steps: In a large skillet with a fitted lid, add the oil over medium high heat. Once hot, add the chicken and cook, flipping once or twice to brown on all sides (don't cook chicken through). Remove to a bowl. Add sausage and cook until browned on both sides. Add to the bowl with the chicken.
Reduce heat to medium and add butter and flour to the pan and stir well, scraping up any leftover browned bits from the pan. Add onion, garlic, celery, and bell peppers and sauté for a 3 minutes.

Add basil, cajun seasoning, diced tomatoes, salt and pepper and stir well to combine. Add chicken broth and rice bring mixture to a gentle boil. Add reserved meat to the pan. Reduce heat, cover pan with fitted lid and cook for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat, and rest with the lid on for 10 minutes. Then gently fluff with a fork and rest again for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Thanksgiving Hand Pies
recipes.note:
Hot water crust cups layered with mashed potato, turkey in gravy and a stuffing lid, finished with cranberry sauce. Leftovers from Thanksgiving dinner work well.
The gravy must be cold and thick, almost a spoonable gel. Thin gravy soaks through the potato into the base and makes soggy bottoms.
Fresh-milled flour works well in hot water crust, with no autolyse needed. Sifting gives smoother walls. Add up to 10 g more water if the dough cracks.
To make ahead, assemble, refrigerate, and bake from cold with 5 extra minutes.
ingredients: 300 g fresh-milled hard white flour, sifted (or all-purpose)
steps: Toss the turkey with the gravy. Keep the turkey mixture, mashed potatoes and stuffing cold. Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and lightly grease a 12-cup muffin tin.

Whisk the flour and salt in a bowl. In a saucepan, bring the water, butter and lard to a simmer until the fat melts. Pour it into the flour and stir with a spoon. When cool enough to handle, knead briefly until smooth.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces of about 43 g. Press each into a cup and up the sides, 3 to 4 mm thick. Work while the dough is warm and keep the rest covered, since it gets crumbly as it cools.
Press about 25 g mashed potatoes into each base. Add about 37 g of the turkey mixture, then top with about 20 g stuffing pressed down like a lid. Brush the crust rims with egg wash.
Bake about 32 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the stuffing tops are crisp.
Rest in the tin 10 minutes so the crust firms up. Run a knife around each pie and lift it out. Top each with a spoonful of cranberry sauce.
